title: Which bars of the tiger graph are wrong?
description: Two students made a table and a bar graph of the number of tigers in India, but some bars do not match the table. Each bar is checked against its table value on the scale, and the wrong bars are redrawn.
teaching_notes: One idea: check every bar against the table by finding the value on the scale. Watch for students who check only the tallest bar.

video_script.why: The child checks each bar of a graph against the table by finding the value on the scale, and redraws the bars that do not match.
video_script.substitution: Find each table value on the scale, compare it with the end of the bar, and redraw the bars that do not match.
video_script.anchor: the table of the number of tigers in India: 2006 1400, 2010 1700, 2014 2200, 2018 3000, 2022 3700, and the bar graph made from it with a few mistakes
video_script.payoff_line: The bars of the first four years are wrong, and the bar of the last year is right

final_answer.value: Mistakes in the bars of 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 (2022 is correct)
final_answer.spoken: the bars of the first four years are wrong, and the bar of the last year is right

maths_rules: 1400 and 1700 lie between 1000 and 2000; 2200 lies just above 2000; 3000 lies on a mark; 3700 lies between 3000 and 4000
book answer: the bars of 2006, 2010, 2014 and 2018 are wrong; 2022 is correct
video_script.design: One idea: find each table value on the scale and compare it with the end of the bar. The table and the graph stay on the board all video.
open_questions: The faulty figure is not in the book text. The video follows the book's answer, that the bars of the first four years are wrong and the last bar is right, and does not claim to say how far each bar is off.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about tigers in India.
<bookmark mark='table'/>Two students noted the number of tigers every four years, from two thousand six.
<bookmark mark='graph'/>They drew a bar graph from the table, but a few bars have mistakes.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which bars are wrong, and how can we fix them?

beats.on_screen: the table and graph stay on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a vertical line with the marks 1000 and 2000; a dot at 1500 halfway between them; the words find the value on the line, then compare with the end of the bar

marks.line: a vertical line with the marks 1000 and 2000 appears
marks.dot: a dot appears halfway between the marks and is labelled 1500
marks.words: the words find the value on the line, then compare with the end of the bar appear

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A bar should end at its number on the side line.
<bookmark mark='dot'/>Fifteen hundred sits halfway between the marks one thousand and two thousand.
<bookmark mark='words'/>To check a bar, find its number on the line and see if the bar ends there.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Given, the table shows fourteen hundred, seventeen hundred and twenty two hundred tigers for the first three years.
<bookmark mark='last'/>It shows three thousand and thirty seven hundred for the last two years.

beats.on_screen: To find: the bars that do not match the table, and the right bars

marks.find: the words the bars that do not match the table are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the bars that do not match the table.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: place each table value on the line: 1400 and 1700 between 1000 and 2000; 2200 just above 2000; 3000 on the mark 3000; 3700 between 3000 and 4000

marks.low: 1400 and 1700 are placed between the marks 1000 and 2000
marks.mid: 2200 is placed just above 2000 and 3000 is placed on its mark
marks.top: 3700 is placed between 3000 and 4000, close to 4000

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step one, place each table number on the side line. Fourteen hundred and seventeen hundred lie between one thousand and two thousand.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twenty two hundred lies a little above two thousand, and three thousand sits on its mark.
<bookmark mark='top'/>Thirty seven hundred lies between three thousand and four thousand, close to four thousand.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: compare the end of each bar with its place; the first four bars do not end at their places; the 2022 bar ends at 3700

marks.four: a cross appears on the first four bars
marks.last: a tick appears on the 2022 bar

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, compare the end of each bar with its place on the line. The first four bars do not end where they should.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last bar ends at thirty seven hundred, so it matches the table.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: redraw the four bars to 1400, 1700, 2200 and 3000; leave the 2022 bar at 3700

marks.redraw: the first four bars are redrawn to 1400, 1700, 2200 and 3000

narration: <bookmark mark='redraw'/>Step three, redraw the four wrong bars to fourteen hundred, seventeen hundred, twenty two hundred and three thousand.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Leave the last bar as it is.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the rises. 1700 - 1400 = 300; 2200 - 1700 = 500; 3000 - 2200 = 800; 3700 - 3000 = 700; every bar is taller than the one before

marks.one: 1700 - 1400 = 300 and 2200 - 1700 = 500 are written between the bars
marks.two: 3000 - 2200 = 800 and 3700 - 3000 = 700 are written between the bars
marks.rise: an arrow shows every bar taller than the one before

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, check the rises. Seventeen hundred take away fourteen hundred is three hundred. Twenty two hundred take away seventeen hundred is five hundred.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Three thousand take away twenty two hundred is eight hundred. Thirty seven hundred take away three thousand is seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='rise'/>Every rise is above zero, so every bar is taller than the one before. This matches the table.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Mistakes in the bars of 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 (2022 is correct)
